findings.summary: G3 run selection could hide a failing run for the same head
findings.rationale: The workflow is triggered only by pull_request (opened/synchronize/reopened, expected base). Candidates must match app, workflow path, check name, event=pull_request, head_sha=H and the recorded PR number. A same-workflow run for H with another event or PR is unknown (unexpected_event_context), not ignored. Within a run the latest run_attempt wins, so earlier failed attempts are not required forever; across runs for the same H, the latest attempt of every run counts (all success required). The review's alternative of turning disagreement into unknown was partly not adopted: a failed or pending latest attempt keeps its real state, so a failure opens a correction batch instead of an infra Blocked. No new workflow layer.
findings.why_no_false_pass: PR-fail/push-success: push runs are not expected under the policy; if one appears it is unknown. Older PR run rerun after a newer run: it belongs to the same H, so its latest attempt (pending/failure) is counted and G3 cannot pass on the newer run alone.
affected_sections: design.md §8 Run/attempt selection, why no false pass, §12

findings.summary: No Red rule for correction attempts or multi-attempt tasks
findings.rationale: Grounded in GAT-03/D01 (Red traces to the same task or later correction) and D26. Every behavior-changing correction attempt (pre_review_g1, G2/G3 batch, base-integration conflict resolution, human return) needs an original Red bound to task/attempt, finding ID(s) and batch ID, with the same three qualifications; each behavior-changing finding in a batch needs at least one Red naming it. Only attempts in H's lineage are eligible; a redo attempt captures its own Red. A unit with no eligible original Red fails G1 and Blocks with original_red_unavailable; replay or reverting code to recapture is not a substitute. Non-behavior corrections use N/A eligibility by actual behavior.
affected_sections: design.md §7 Red units, attempt eligibility, missing evidence; §9 Batch

findings.summary: Rebase/force-push onto a new base breaks Red lineage
findings.rationale: The force-with-lease retry example is removed; the idempotent example is now a same-SHA ordinary fast-forward push. During a controlled active run the feature branch is updated only by fast-forward push. Base integration is a local merge commit in the Implementer worktree, not a GitHub PR merge and with no merge permission, so prior attempt commits stay ancestors of H. No rebase, squash or force-push; a non-FF rejection is failed and Blocked, never auto-rebased. If history is rewritten externally (new H not a descendant of the recorded head), lineage-based Red eligibility is invalidated and G1 Blocks with history_rewritten; no evidence is fabricated. This is a rule for the controlled run, not a repository-wide ban.
affected_sections: design.md §4 retry, Branch history; §7 history rewritten; §8 base integration

findings.summary: CI jobs did not enforce the skip policy
findings.rationale: The same collection/skip/failure policy applies locally and in each CI job through test-only configuration owned by T1.1: pyproject pytest settings (--strict-markers, xfail_strict) and tests/conftest.py with a single only_on(platform) marker plus a session-finish check. Zero collected, any skip not produced by only_on on a non-owning platform, xfail/xpass, or a job platform mismatch fails the session. The skip reason text is never evidence, so the review's suggested reason-based check was not adopted. A Linux-owned case that skips on Linux fails the Linux job. No production hook and no registry.

findings.summary: pr_ensure could adopt the wrong PR
findings.rationale: Before the external call, the prepared op persists the expected identity (repo, head repo+branch, current head SHA, base repo+branch) and a unique operation marker. The pre-create query covers all open PRs for the head branch, with any base. Exactly one full match is reused and recorded as origin=existing, without claiming it was created. Any mismatch, including the same branch with a wrong base, Blocks with no new creation. Recovery after an unknown create needs marker plus full identity for origin=created. Marker without identity, or identity without marker, is Blocked for a human.

The Pass package is a human-readable projection of feature state produced by assess. It is not a second authority and cannot pass on its own. Per formal ORC-05 it lists version_key, PR identity with origin, head/base, gate reasons and result IDs/digests, findings, limitations, the policy source (rules, or approved_policy with the workflow.yaml digest and policy_change ID), github_rules_verified, publication status and receipts, the pass observation seq, and acceptance=pending.

The first slice's scope_change stops the whole run (d4). Continuing only the unaffected work is explicitly deferred to S2 and does not count as complete. Coverage, spec-delta §9, design §1, the tasks deferred list and W-C now agree. The AC class stays WF, so counts are unchanged.

N/A eligibility follows the actual behavior of the diff, as judged by the independent Reviewer. There is no blanket ban by file name or type: comment-only config or test edits may be eligible, while changed config values, test assertions or migrations are not. spec-delta §4 states that D26 is not narrowed.

findings.summary: No task step owns the formal OpenSpec sync
findings.rationale: T0.1 step 1 runs after D11 and before commit B. It adopts a complete formal spec baseline rather than the candidate delta alone, because that delta relies on the unadopted d45-02 baseline. D11 names both deltas by sha256; the four formal specs are composed from the formal text, all d45-02 items not overridden, and these overrides. A per-requirement/AC source mapping is recorded, and an independent reviewer checks the result. Any semantic divergence returns to the user, with no self-approval. Step 2 supersedes the old D40 formal design/tasks/validation so they do not compete with the adopted plan. Assignments bind spec digests from B.

Integration triggers are GitHub mergeable=false, a Reviewer finding of incompatibility, or a human revise decision. mergeable=null is treated as pending and Blocks at timeout. Integration joins the same-version correction batch (FIN-03; one round when dispatched). It is a local git merge commit in the Implementer worktree, not a GitHub PR merge, and needs no merge permission. When H is unchanged, G3 reuse records its applicability reason (formal AC-G17). Not adopted: dropping the head-only Green re-run when there is no trigger. That rebinding was closed under D51-R02, and the text now says plainly that it only rebinds the base and does not verify integration.

findings.summary: Checks not tied to their own tested SHA
findings.rationale: Each job uploads a uniquely named artifact tested-sha-<job>-<run_attempt> holding run_id, run_attempt, job, check name and tested SHA. A check counts only if every field matches and the SHA equals H. A missing artifact or any mismatch is unknown and never passes.

resolve_operation is record-only and performs no external write. --bind needs a fresh read that matches the persisted expected identity. --not-delivered needs human evidence of non-delivery, and an absent-query observation alone is rejected. Afterwards the bounded retry rules (at most 2 extra per op) still apply, and pr_ensure still runs its pre-create query.

The policy file is the repo-root workflow.yaml, loopctl's gate policy file, which is distinct from the GitHub workflow .github/workflows/loopctl-ci.yml. It records the required checks, the GitHub workflow path and blob digest, source: head, empty exceptions and the evidence command IDs. T1.1 creates and owns it, and later changes need a new policy_change. The policy_change binds its digest, and a GitHub workflow digest mismatch at H is unknown and Blocked.
